prediction.raw: 0 I think it's wrong to stop throwing the bell-ball for your cat just because they won't throw it back. As a responsible and caring pet owner, it's great that you were engaging in play with your cat in the first place. Cats often enjoy chasing and pouncing on toys, and it's a great way to provide them with exercise and mental stimulation. Just because your cat doesn't throw the ball back doesn't mean they're not enjoying the game or benefiting from the interaction. Cats are natural predators, and chasing a toy is a great way for them to express their instincts and have fun. By stopping the game, you may be depriving your cat of a source of enjoyment and exercise. Instead, you could try adapting the game to your cat's preferences and abilities. For example, you could try using a different type of toy or varying the way you throw the bell-ball to keep the game interesting and engaging for your cat. This way, you can continue to provide your cat with a fun and stimulating experience, even if they don't throw the ball back.
